Project Overview

This project explores the security vulnerabilities in Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), which are critical components in Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and SCADA environments. PLCs control everything from manufacturing equipment to critical infrastructure like power grids and water treatment facilities.

Panasonic FP-XH C30T PLC - Target device for this research

Project Goals

  1. Reconnaissance: Identify PLC models, protocols, and network configurations
  2. Vulnerability Analysis: Discover authentication weaknesses and unpatched CVEs
  3. Exploitation: Develop proof-of-concept attacks
  4. Defense: Document mitigation strategies and secure configuration practices

Target Environment

Device: Panasonic FP-XH C30T PLC
Protocols: Modbus TCP, Proprietary Panasonic protocols
Network: Isolated lab environment

Attack Surface

Communication Protocols

  • Modbus TCP (502)
  • Ethernet/IP
  • Proprietary vendor protocols
  • Web-based configuration interfaces

Common Vulnerabilities

  • Default credentials
  • Unencrypted communications
  • Lack of authentication
  • Firmware vulnerabilities
  • Physical access exploitation

Research Phases

Phase 1: Network Discovery (In Progress)

  • Port scanning and service enumeration
  • Protocol identification
  • Firmware version detection

Phase 2: Protocol Analysis

  • Traffic capture and analysis
  • Command structure reverse engineering
  • Authentication mechanism study

Phase 3: Exploitation

  • Authentication bypass attempts
  • Command injection testing
  • Ladder logic manipulation
  • Denial of service testing

Phase 4: Post-Exploitation

  • Persistence mechanisms
  • Lateral movement
  • Data exfiltration
  • Physical process manipulation

Security Implications

Successful exploitation of PLCs can lead to:

  • Physical damage: Equipment destruction
  • Safety hazards: Process disruption in critical systems
  • Production loss: Manufacturing downtime
  • Supply chain attacks: Compromised industrial processes

Defense Strategies

  1. Network Segmentation

    • Air-gapped ICS networks
    • Firewall rules between IT/OT
    • DMZ for remote access

  2. Authentication & Access Control

    • Change default credentials
    • Implement role-based access control (RBAC)
    • Multi-factor authentication where supported

  3. Monitoring & Detection

    • Protocol anomaly detection
    • Baseline normal operations
    • Alert on unauthorized changes

  4. Patch Management

    • Regular firmware updates
    • Testing updates in lab environment
    • Vendor security advisories

Current Status

🔴 In Progress - Currently in reconnaissance phase, documenting network protocols and device behavior.
